# Mutation transcript — P5 Task B2 (block-time custody + observatory rollup)

Durable mutation evidence for Task B2's daemon additions: migrations
00015 (block_headers) / 00016 (observatory_points), the store surface
(`internal/store/p5_block_headers.go`, `internal/store/p5_observatory.go`),
the indexer's per-round custody pass + retry sweep
(`cmd/indexer/blocktimes.go`), and `cmd/backfill-blocktimes`.

The mutant SPECS were written into the test-file headers
(`p5_block_headers_test.go`, `p5_observatory_test.go`,
`cmd/indexer/blocktimes_test.go`) BEFORE the corresponding implementation
loops; m4 was added with the integrator's mid-flight correction (rollup
source = the newest COMPLETE batch, never raw derived state) before its
implementation change landed. This wave's tree rules forbid committing, so
"committed before the loop" is satisfied at file level, not commit level —
the integrator lands the whole tree.

## m1 — fabricated time (the writer stamps now() instead of the header time)

Spec (test-file header, before the loop): `UpsertBlockHeader` stores a clock
of its own instead of the caller's chain-asserted header timestamp.

Cut: in `p5_block_headers.go`, the bound argument
`w.ChainID, w.Block, w.Hash, w.Time` becomes
`w.ChainID, w.Block, w.Hash, time.Now().Unix()` (plus the `"time"` import).

Mutated-file sha256:
`f8bd51dcc6c8b569e4811e03c84d58958c14d50b7941b57a67c81a320853cf22`

### Kill (store custody suite, exit 1)

KILLED by the designed killer `TestUpsertBlockHeaderStoresChainAssertedTimeExactly`
— its fixture time (2021-04-13, `1618300800`) is years from any test-run
clock, and the drift assertion (`abs(now() - block_time) > 24h`) closes the
window where a clock could impersonate a header. One collateral kill
(`TestUpsertBlockHeaderIdempotentAndRefusesDivergence`: an identical
re-write stops being identical when the writer invents the time). Every
other custody test stayed GREEN.

```
--- FAIL: TestUpsertBlockHeaderStoresChainAssertedTimeExactly (0.33s)
        Error:       Not equal:
                     expected: 1618300800
                     actual  : 1785471433
        Messages:    block_time must be the header's OWN timestamp, exactly as given —
                     a writer stamping any clock of its own is the fabricated-time mutant
--- FAIL: TestUpsertBlockHeaderIdempotentAndRefusesDivergence (0.72s)
        Error:       Not equal:
                     expected: 1724000000
                     actual  : 1785471433
FAIL    github.com/kaselunt/solvent/internal/store      5.053s
```

Restore verified: `p5_block_headers.go` sha256 back to
`d281570a…74e8d624`.

The cmd-side half of the same law (the daemon pass forwarding the fetched
header's time, bit-exact, into the write) is pinned separately by
`TestHeaderCustodyWritesChainAssertedHeaderTime` against a fake store.

## m2 — a fetch failure blocks the ingest round

Spec (test-file header, before the loop): the pass's fetch-failure arm
aborts the whole pass, so one dead header fetch starves every later block
and unit in the round — the exact inversion of the failure law ("a header
fetch failure NEVER blocks or fails the ingest round; rows are simply
absent").

Cut: in `cmd/indexer/blocktimes.go` `pass()`, the outcome switch arm
`case custodyFailed: failed++` becomes `case custodyFailed: return`.

Mutated-file sha256:
`e314e7f7dddec12fa9dc184c37bd5fb49eab9c33f7607525dbcb5435ecd6a8d2`

### Kill (daemon pass suite, exit 1)

KILLED by the designed killer `TestHeaderCustodyFetchFailureNeverBlocksTheRound`
— the injected failure at block 100 must leave block 110 custodied in the
SAME round and the watermark advanced; under the mutant the round dies at
the failure. One collateral kill
(`TestHeaderCustodyRetrySweepClosesTransientHoles`: the abort also skips
watermark advancement, `0x64`=100 vs expected `0xc8`=200). Every other
custody-pass test — refusal discipline, cap/carry-over, clamp, resume —
stayed GREEN.

```
--- FAIL: TestHeaderCustodyFetchFailureNeverBlocksTheRound (0.00s)
        Error:       "[]" should have 1 item(s), but has 0
        Messages:    the failed block's row stays ABSENT — absence is the honest state
--- FAIL: TestHeaderCustodyRetrySweepClosesTransientHoles (0.00s)
        Error:       Not equal:
                     expected: 0xc8
                     actual  : 0x64
FAIL    github.com/kaselunt/solvent/cmd/indexer 1.223s
```

Restore verified: `blocktimes.go` sha256 back to `3327adbf…e27530e23`.

Note the daemon-level guarantee is also structural: `pass()` returns
nothing, is called outside the worker-step composition, and never touches
`anyAdvanced` or the health surface — no return path exists by which it
could fail a round even unmutated.

## m3 — rollup non-idempotent (double-tick doubles a bucket)

Spec (test-file header, before the loop): the upsert's conflict arm
ACCUMULATES instead of replacing.

Cut: in `p5_observatory.go`, the conflict arm's
`total_collateral = EXCLUDED.total_collateral` /
`total_debt = EXCLUDED.total_debt` become
`observatory_points.total_collateral + EXCLUDED.total_collateral` /
`observatory_points.total_debt + EXCLUDED.total_debt`.

Mutated-file sha256:
`2867f1522bc5a2019f7bf9a4242338147b3b9776d3823d150bcc1b1e1a715653`

### Kill (store rollup suite, exit 1)

KILLED by `TestWriteObservatoryPointsIdempotentPerBucket`, and by NOTHING
else — the arithmetic is the proof: batch A carries collateral 3e11, batch
B (same bucket) 5e11; the mutant writes 3e11+5e11=8e11 where the law
requires the refresh to REPLACE with 5e11. (The same-batch double-tick leg
cannot catch this mutant on its own — the batch-id guard skips the update
entirely — which is exactly why the test's second leg re-ticks with a NEW
batch.)

```
--- FAIL: TestWriteObservatoryPointsIdempotentPerBucket (0.24s)
        Error:       Not equal:
                     expected: "500000000000"
                     actual  : "800000000000"
FAIL    github.com/kaselunt/solvent/internal/store      2.148s
```

Restore verified: `p5_observatory.go` sha256 back to `a151a446…0aa244318`.

## m4 — a point computed from raw derived state instead of the batch

Spec (test-file header, added with the integrator's mid-flight correction,
before the corresponding change landed): the writer's totals sourced from
live `position_balances` sums at tick time rather than copied from
`risk_batch_aggregates` — bypassing the batch pipeline's gates, refusals,
price snapshot and stamps, and able to disagree with the public Book.

Cut: in `p5_observatory.go`'s INSERT…SELECT, `a.total_collateral,
a.total_debt` become correlated `COALESCE(sum(position_balances.amount)…)`
subqueries per side.

Mutated-file sha256:
`9f2e844754b6c6ebe9b74c54251fcc71456b6264e9dbabca3536841ce4231f85`

### Kill (store rollup suite, exit 1)

KILLED by the designed killer
`TestObservatoryPointsObserveTheBatchNotDerivedState`, whose fixture makes
the two sources DISAGREE — a live derived debt balance of
999999999999999999 against the batch's audited 100000000000 — and requires
the batch's number verbatim. Two collateral kills where derived state is
EMPTY while the batch carries totals (the mutant writes 0 — the "most
dangerous zero" shape).

```
--- FAIL: TestWriteObservatoryPointsObservesNewestCompleteBatch (0.38s)
        Error:       expected: "300000000000"  actual: "0"
--- FAIL: TestWriteObservatoryPointsIdempotentPerBucket (0.28s)
        Error:       expected: "100000000000"  actual: "0"
--- FAIL: TestObservatoryPointsObserveTheBatchNotDerivedState (0.34s)
        Error:       expected: "100000000000"  actual: "999999999999999999"
FAIL    github.com/kaselunt/solvent/internal/store
```

Restore verified: `p5_observatory.go` sha256 back to `a151a446…0aa244318`.
